outcome.notes: C-0001 resolved as witness A-attribution-W01: the SSRC working paper is the arXiv 2508.00838 preprint by Strauss, Yang, O'Reilly, Rosenblat and Moure, dated 2025-06-27 on arXiv and on its Rogue Scholar DOI record, later published in Data & Policy 8, e15 (online 2026-04-28, DOI 10.1017/dap.2026.10064). It precedes every claim it bears on and is an anticipation. C-0002 resolved as witness A-attribution-W02: arXiv 2510.04226 v1, 2025-10-05, by Wright, Masud, Moore, Yadav, Antoniak, Christensen, Park and Augenstein. It measures epistemic diversity and has no bearing on attribution; it is recorded against two B-collapse claims (PRED-199.A1, as a mechanism-level disconfirmation in another domain; PRED-857.F1, as the method carried out). The main session should check that placement against the B-collapse reader's file to avoid a duplicate. Class-level exclusion: the query-resolution forecasts (PRED-140.A1, PRED-141.A1 to A5, PRED-768.A1 to A5) forecast what a query will surface about the archive's own terms. Outside research on source bias bears only on their premise, so none was attached; their test is the archive's own capture. The same holds for the claims about the archive's own entities and deposits (Lee Sharks, Mary Lee, Pearl, the MacArthur bios, the Dodecad and similar), which no outside study can witness. A-attribution-W12 (BuzzStream) is the one disconfirmation in theme A: it breaks the first link of PRED-615.B3. The same post would support a component of PRED-1091.B3 (the platform's opt-out does not control use); it was not attached there because a witness carries one direction, and the main session may add a second link as its own witness if wanted. Several witnesses are industry or vendor studies (Ahrefs, BuzzStream, SE Ranking via SEJ, Chartbeat via SEJ); their class is recorded as post or news, and their vendor status is listed under unverified. Two primaries were refused or gated (bbc.com blocked; Chartbeat report gated; SE Ranking page empty); the witnesses rest on the copies named in checked. Quotes are as returned by WebFetch, which quotes in segments of under 125 characters; quotes the tool gave only in paraphrase were left out. No memory facts were used in this pass.

outcome.notes: Scope: 166 claims in the theme; most are narrative, internal-protocol or archive-specific (Assembly Chorus, SPXI, RES, Glas function, Bead Count tiers) with no external analogue, and were not searched. Searched lines: cross-model and longitudinal convergence (857.F1, 803.B2), alignment and diversity (107.G1), recursive-training collapse and real-data thresholds (782.A7, 635.F1, 1573.F4), machine-text predictability (110.A1, 110.F2), code monoculture (199.A1, 199.A2, 199.F1), chat data (856.B1, 856.F1), academic discourse (476.A2, 476.A3, 1540.F3), mediation design (779.F4), diversity benchmarks (855.F1), hallucination regularity and seeding (1287.E1, 1287.E3, 21.B2), evaluator gaming and humanizers (741.B2, 1540.B1), entity tail (782.A5), adoption (124.B1), RAG self-retrieval (923.B2, 1088.B1), poetic jailbreaks (1205.F2, 1251.B1). Disconfirmations: B-collapse-W25 (Kosch et al., CHI writing: prose did not homogenize, vocabulary grew more varied) against 476.A2's academic-discourse component; it sits beside B-collapse-W22, W23 and W24, which support that component in biomedicine, natural science and Scopus-wide. B-collapse-W05 (Fortier, Chen & West, EMNLP 2026) locates output homogeneity in pretraining with alignment as amplifier, which tells against safety pressure as the origin named by 803.B2; it also bears on 107.G1, whose predicted direction (instruct below base) it leaves standing while contesting RLHF as the source, so it was not linked there; the main session may wish to add a 107.G1 link with that scope. On 855.F1: NoveltyBench (W29) predates the claim and is a benchmark of output diversity; the claim's sentence that no such benchmark exists in any deployed evaluation framework stands only on a narrow reading of 'deployed'. Recorded as method support; the operator may rule it a disconfirmation of that sentence. W-0003 (de Rooij & Biskjaer) may also bear on PRED-779.F4 as method in part: a reanalysis of existing AI-creativity studies with a moderator (task constraint); the claim's moderator is mediation design, so the fit is partial. It does not bear on 476.A3's population-level trajectory. Anticipations: most witnesses predate their claims (the collapse literature from 2023–2024, the alignment-diversity literature from 2023–2025). After-registration witnesses: W02 (857.F1, 803.B2), W05, W19 (199.A2), W25 (476.A2, 1540.F3), and W37's arXiv version. Evidence classes needing care: W37 is a company research post by Graphite's officers, with an arXiv version; W34 is news reporting a figure from an integrity-software founder whose method is not described; W20 is a vendor announcement. Quotes: WebFetch returns verbatim fragments of at most about 120 characters, so long abstracts are quoted in pieces; every quote was requested character for character from the fetched page. The summarizer's paraphrase was never used as a quote. Not resolved: PRED-782.A7 part (3), the critical α in 0.05–0.15, has threshold existence results (W12, W13) and no value in the claim's terms; Garg et al. (2509.22341) give an optimal ratio near 0.618 for linear interpolation, a different quantity, logged as excluded. PRED-199.A1's generational SSDI decline has no direct measurement in code; W03 and W02 show generational decline in text. PRED-107.G3 (human-rated slop and signed deviation): Shaib et al. relate slop to coherence and relevance and do not test deviation. Prose rule: two verbatim quotes (W23, W27) contain a phrase the prose rules bar outside quotation; they are left as found.

outcome.notes: 142 claims were read. Most are internal to the archive (self-referential tests, Space Ark transforms, future fictional citations, capture batteries on the archive's own entities) and have no outside test; outside evidence was sought for about twenty that name a measurable effect or a general mechanism. Every witness recorded here bears as mechanism, method or component; none bears on a claim as a whole, because the claims concern the archive's own deposits and the outside research does not. Most witnesses predate their claims and will order as anticipations; those after registration are E-execution-W02 (2026-10-02, after PRED-139.F1 2026-05-29), W09 and W10 (2026-05-13, after PRED-42.B1 2026-03-26), W20 (2026-04-06, after PRED-218.F1 and PRED-219.F1, 2026-01-03). W03 (2026-05-17), W23 (2026-05-25) and W28 (2026-05-11) fall weeks before their claims and are anticipations. The order script computes this; the reader's reckoning is only a guide. PRED-194.A1 falsifier (c): checked 2026-10-30, the official OWASP LLM Top 10 is still the 2025 edition and no NIST AI 100-2 edition after E2025 was found, so the falsifier has not fired; window runs to 2028-06-12. The NIST E2025 definitions of prompt injection could not be read through the fetch tool (sections 3.3, 3.4 and the glossary fell outside the returned text); a reader with the PDF should quote them before any NIST witness is recorded. Three sources are recorded twice in opposite directions on different components: Souly et al. (W05 supports, W06 disconfirms the corpus-share term of PRED-127.B1), Negation Neglect (W09 supports for the training layer, W10 disconfirms for the in-context stage of PRED-42.B1), FABLES (W15 supports method, W16 disconfirms the 'current benchmarks do not test' component of PRED-34.F2). The main session may prefer to merge them. PRED-176.F1 has a split record: GEO (W21) supports that presentation changes visibility; Wan et al. (W22) and Vishwakarma et al. (W23) find relevance dominates and stylistic or formatting cues matter little. Meeus et al. 2024 (W07) is already cited inside the archive at PRED-1384.F4. The fetch tool caps quotes at about 125 characters, so findings are short fragments; each was returned by the tool as verbatim from the page named. The GEO quote keeps the LaTeX '$40\%$' as the arXiv abstract served it. Peer-reviewed venues known only from search results (ICML, ICLR, USENIX, NeurIPS, ACL, KDD, Findings of EMNLP, COLM) are named in source.venue and listed in checked.unverified; the evidence_class of those witnesses is set to preprint, the version actually read. The main session may raise a class after confirming the venue page.
